title: Multi-objective Large Language Model Alignment with Hierarchical Experts
claim: Single jack-of-all-trades or isolated experts trace a suboptimal trade-off curve; hierarchical experts cover and approach the full Pareto frontier.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, shared obj A/B axes, legends above each
description: Two side-by-side 2-D plots with obj A on the vertical axis and obj B on the horizontal axis. The left panel is a conceptual sketch. A black solid curve is labeled Jack-of-all-trades. Several dashed expert curves in green, yellow, pink and red sit beneath a thick green-to-orange gradient curve labeled Ours, Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts. Teal dashed arrows point outward to mark each specialized direction. The right panel shows nested blue shaded regions for base models (stars), model soups (squares), LoRA experts (crosses) and router experts (circles). A gray dashed Pareto frontier bounds them. Preference weights such as [0,1], [1/4,3/4], [1/2,1/2], [3/4,1/4] and [1,0] are in green, with teal arrows pointing to the frontier. The eye goes first to the gradient curve on the left, then to the layered blue region on the right.
caption: (Left) HoE decomposes the multi-objective alignment problem into a series of single-preference subproblems, each handled by a specialized expert. (Right) HoE employs hierarchical experts, integrating LoRA and router experts to approach the optimal Pareto frontier.
abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) to simultaneously satisfy multiple objectives remains a significant challenge, especially given the diverse and often conflicting nature of human preferences. Existing alignment methods struggle to balance trade-offs effectively, often requiring costly retraining or yielding suboptimal results across the Pareto frontier of preferences. In this paper, we introduce \textit{HoE}(Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts), a \textit{lightweight}, \textit{parameter-efficient}, and \textit{plug-and-play} approach that eliminates the need for model training, while enabling LLMs to adapt across the entire Pareto frontier and accommodate diverse user preferences. In particular, \textit{HoE} consists of three hierarchical components: LoRA Experts, Router Experts and Preference Routing, reaching optimal Pareto frontiers and achieving a trade-off between parameter size, training cost, and performance. We evaluate \textit{HoE} across various tasks on 14 objectives and 200 different preferences among 6 benchmarks, demonstrating superior performance over 15 recent baselines. Code is available in the supplementary materials.
